FinTech Funding October 2026: Indian FinTechs raise USD 76 million across 6 deals
The largest deal of the month came from Even, which raised USD 50 million from Khosla Ventures and Alpha Wave Global, followed by StockGro and Fission Labs, which raised USD 10 million each.
Shrishti Sharma
ETBFSI

Indian FinTechs raised USD 76 million across six equity funding rounds in October 2026, according to data collated by Tracxn.
The month witnessed funding activity across healthcare and insurance technology, investment and trading platforms, blockchain-based financial infrastructure, lending and debt resolution, and cross-border payments .
The largest deal of the month came from Even, a healthcare platform offering managed care services, doctor consultations and health insurance solutions, which raised USD 50 million in a Series B round from Khosla Ventures and Alpha Wave Global.
This was followed by StockGro, a stock market advisory and research platform, which raised USD 10 million in a Series B round from Aart Corporate Advisors.
Advt
Another notable transaction was Fission Labs , a financial technology company building blockchain-based infrastructure for tokenised investment funds, which raised USD 10 million in a Series A round. The round saw participation from Pantera Capital, Circle, Borderless Capital, New Form Capital, gCC, Manhattan Venture Partners, Reflexive Capital and Lattice, along with angel investors Ari Rubenstein and Anthony Scaramucci.
Together, the three largest transactions accounted for USD 70 million, or nearly 92 per cent of the total funding raised during October.
Among the other deals during the month:
Tradl, an artificial intelligence-powered trading platform, raised USD 4 million in a seed funding round from Stellaris Venture Partners.
CredFix, a financial technology platform connecting lenders and borrowers, particularly those facing financial distress, raised USD 2 million in a seed round from Stargazer Growth and Tanglin Venture Partners.
Saber, a provider of stablecoin-powered cross-border payment infrastructure, also raised an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round from Tether and Titan.
Funding activity in October was lower than the previous month, with total funding declining to USD 76 million across six deals, compared with USD 111 million across 10 deals in September 2026.

articles.snippet: Funding and M&A Roundup: Green Genius Raises $72.5 Million Via Green Bonds Mercom Capital Group
articles.text:
November 11, 2026
Staff
Solar , Storage
Renewable energy project developer Green Genius has completed a €65 million (~$72.5 million) green bond issue to refinance existing subordinated construction loans. The bonds have a four-year maturity and carry a floating interest rate based on the three-month Euro Interbank Offered Rate (EURIBOR) plus 8% annually. They are expected to be admitted to trading on the Sustainable Bond List of Nasdaq Stockholm.
FluoRok, a U.K.-based company developing materials for applications including lithium-ion battery electrolytes , has raised $30 million in an oversubscribed Series A funding round to scale its manufacturing platform and expand fluorochemical production. Orano Venture Fund and Supernova Invest led the funding round, with participation from Bidra Innovation Ventures.
RadianX, a perovskite solar module manufacturer formerly known as California Perovskite Technology, has raised $9 million in combined venture and project financing to scale production of its certified perovskite solar modules. SOSV and Twynam co-led the seed funding round, with participation from One Small Planet, Sahsen Ventures, Avila VC, California Innovation Fund, quantumEDGE, Riceberg Ventures, and Alumni Ventures.
ARRAY Technologies, a provider of solar tracking technology, fixed-tilt products, and foundation solutions, and Shoals Technologies Group , a provider of electrical balance-of-system solutions for utility-scale solar and battery storage, have entered into a definitive agreement for a stock-for-stock merger. Under the merger agreement, ARRAY will be the legal acquirer and corporate parent of the combined company, and Shoals shareholders will receive 1.6931 ARRAY shares for each Shoals share they own.
SOLV Energy, a company that provides construction, operation, and maintenance services for large-scale solar and battery storage projects, has acquired Texas-based ASB Energy Services, a contractor specializing in substation foundations, civil construction, and battery energy storage infrastructure, for approximately $45 million. The transaction comprises $36 million in cash and $9 million in shares of SOLV Energy’s Class A common stock, excluding customary closing adjustments.

Eli Radiopharma: Nearly $60 Million Series A Financing To Advance Radiopharmaceutical Pipeline Toward Clinical Development
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:27 AM
Eli Radiopharma: Nearly $60 Million Series A Financing To Advance Radiopharmaceutical Pipeline Toward Clinical Development
Eli Radiopharma has raised nearly $60 million (RMB 400 million) in Series A financing to advance its radiopharmaceutical pipeline toward clinical development. The funding will support preclinical research, regulatory submissions, early-stage clinical studies, and the expansion of the company’s research and development capabilities.
Huagai Capital led the financing round, with Bayland Capital serving as co-lead investor. Additional participants included Boyu Ventures, Delian Capital, InnoPinnacle Fund, Haibang Venture, Bairui Capital, Shenzhen Angel FOF Management, and Grand Flight Investment.
Existing shareholders CSPC & Growth Bio Fund, Huaige Capital, KHK Fund, Longfeng Venture, Hongsheng Capital, Bioclub Fund, and Skyfield Capital also participated in the financing.
Eli Radiopharma plans to allocate the proceeds toward preclinical research, investigational new drug applications, and early-stage clinical development. The company will also strengthen its research platforms, recruit additional talent, expand clinical operations, and pursue business development opportunities.
Founded in 2024, Eli Radiopharma focuses on developing radiopharmaceutical products that combine molecular targeting with radionuclide technology. Its pipeline includes diagnostic and therapeutic candidates designed to address unmet medical needs in oncology and neurological diseases.
The company has advanced multiple programs targeting novel molecular mechanisms through lead discovery, laboratory validation, and animal studies. Several candidates are approaching investigational new drug submissions, representing an important transition from early research toward human clinical testing.
Radiopharmaceuticals combine targeting molecules with radioactive isotopes to identify or treat diseased tissue. Therapeutic radioligands are designed to deliver radiation directly to tumors while limiting exposure to surrounding healthy tissue. Related diagnostic imaging agents can help physicians identify appropriate patients, evaluate disease progression, and monitor treatment responses.
The financing also reflects growing international interest in radiopharmaceutical innovation originating in China. Global pharmaceutical companies have increasingly explored opportunities involving novel molecular targets, therapeutic radionuclides, and expanded clinical applications.
Eli Radiopharma’s investors identified these areas as important drivers of future industry growth, particularly as radiopharmaceutical technologies move into additional cancer indications and other therapeutic applications.
The company’s longer-term strategy includes building a globally competitive pipeline capable of serving patients in international markets, including the U.S. and Europe. Its immediate priorities involve completing preclinical development, meeting regulatory requirements, and advancing differentiated candidates into clinical studies.
The Series A financing provides Eli Radiopharma with additional resources to move its lead programs closer to clinical validation while expanding the infrastructure needed to support a broader radiopharmaceutical development portfolio.

The company grew revenue by approximately 800% year over year in 2026 and will use the financing to expand its go-to-market organization and accelerate development of its enterprise AI Control Center and Deep Hat models and add-ons.

Meet Kindo video
As autonomous agents spread through the enterprise and their numbers swell into the thousands, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance teams struggle to control risks and costs without a centralized tool that can discover, observe, and control the entire enterprise AI footprint. Every time a company lets an AI agent access data, update a customer record, approve a request, or change a production system, it delegates authority. The same permissions that let an agent get work done can let it expose sensitive data, make changes outside company policy, disrupt a critical workflow, or rack up huge inference costs.
"Agent builders from the AI labs, hyperscalers, and thousands of startups make it easy to deploy powerful agents across the business," said Ron Williams, founder and CEO of Kindo. "What's missing is the tooling that lets an organization centrally control how those agents are built, what data they can reach, where that data can go, and what they cost, while also allowing support teams to reach in and fix an agent at any hour. That gap is why the teams responsible for supporting and controlling Al are rightfully putting the brakes on Al transformation."
Kindo gives organizations control of the AI agents already running across their operations. It starts with discovery, uncovering shadow AI and mapping where agents are in use, then brings their activity, access, costs, and outcomes into one view. The teams that must support and control AI, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance, get a single set of controls: what employees can do with an agent, what an agent can touch, how it behaves around the clock, and what it costs. The result is an AI Operations Center, SOC- and NOC-style monitoring and intervention for AI, where those teams eliminate risk, drive down cost, and make sure AI delivers measurable outcomes.
Implementation is turnkey and is run by the IT operations staff an organization already has. Teams connect the agents, data sources, and AI models already in use, and from that moment everything is discovered, observed, and controlled from one place. Kindo's gateways govern and audit every call an agent makes to connected data, tools, and approved models. Identity controls apply the organization's existing permissions to people and agents alike, with the option to tighten them centrally. articles.title: Bay Raises $50 Million to Stop AI Agents From Making Dangerous Decisions Inside Companies
articles.snippet: Bay Raises $50 Million to Stop AI Agents From Making Dangerous Decisions Inside Companies https://ascendants.in/
articles.text:
Bay Raises $50 Million to Stop AI Agents From Making Dangerous Decisions Inside Companies
Epil Bodra
| November 11 | Business Stories , Funding Feed
Share
Cybersecurity startup Bay has emerged from stealth with $50 million in funding , just nine months after its founding, as businesses face growing security risks from autonomous AI agents operating across corporate systems.
The company, founded in early 2026 by former Israeli intelligence and cybersecurity professionals, has developed technology designed to detect and block potentially harmful actions by AI agents, including those operating with legitimate access permissions.
The funding includes a $37 million Series A led by Battery Ventures , with participation from Micron Ventures, Microsoft’s venture capital arm M12, and Wiz CEO Assaf Rappaport. Bay also disclosed an earlier $13 million seed round backed by YL Ventures and Striker.
Cisco Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel and former Zscaler Chief Strategy Officer Manoj Apte are among the company’s private investors.
Bay was established by CEO Yuval Zacharia, Chief Product Officer Aner Morag , and Vice President of Research and Development Boris Danilovich.
The founders identified a critical security problem after one of their own AI coding agents attempted to expose a cloud environment to the public internet while completing a test.
The agent had not been compromised, nor was it acting under instructions from an attacker. Instead, it was using authorized permissions to accomplish its assigned task, potentially creating a serious security vulnerability in the process.
That experience became the foundation for Bay’s approach to AI security, which focuses on preventing dangerous actions even when an agent is functioning as intended.
Unlike traditional security systems that primarily focus on unauthorized access or malicious activity, Bay examines what an AI agent is attempting to accomplish and whether its actions could violate an organization’s security policies.
Its platform discovers AI agents operating across corporate environments and analyzes their activities within the context of an entire session, including their assigned objectives and previous actions.
Based on that information, the system can approve an action, block it, or refer it for human authorization. Bay says these decisions occur locally within milliseconds, allowing permitted operations to continue without disrupting workflows.
The technology supports AI assistants, coding agents, custom-built agents, and the tools they use across employee devices, cloud infrastructure, and software-as-a-service applications.
Bay also claims its platform can be deployed in under five minutes using existing corporate security infrastructure, without installing additional persistent endpoint agents or network proxies.
The company says its technology is already being used by dozens of enterprise customers across finance, insurance, manufacturing, media, and technology.
Wix, ClickUp, Micron, and Peloton are among its named customers. Micron is also participating in the company’s latest funding round through Micron Ventures.
Zacharia told Calcalist that Bay’s rapid fundraising was supported by early customer demand and revenue growth. She said the company generated millions in revenue during its first quarter of sales, although an exact figure was not disclosed.
